sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Commodity Trade in Whole and Skimmed Milk Powder

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales (Luxembourg Companies Act of 10 August 1915, as amended), Articles 1, 2, 5, 9-13, 26-28 and Articles 100-1 et seq. (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003 on the organisation of the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 4 place de la Tour, L-2416 Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation and articles of association (acte constitutif / statuts), deposited electronically with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum fully subscribed and paid-up share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into shares with a minimum par value of EUR 1. Cash contributions must be credited to a blocking account at a Luxembourg credit institution and may be released only after RCS registration; non-cash contributions require a statutory auditor's report and full payment at execution of the notarial deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the founding shareholder(s) at the first constituent meeting, that the draft notarial deed of incorporation is approved and that the subscriber set out therein subscribes to and fully pays up the Company's share capital amounting to EUR 12,000 (twelve thousand euros). RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company is fixed at [Street and City], Luxembourg. RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed as manager (gérant), with sole executive authority to bind the Company within the limits of the corporate purpose, law and statutes. RESOLVED that the manager and each authorized RCS agent shall complete all filings, open bank accounts, arrange publication in RESA, and that this resolution remains effective until the first ordinary general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability check and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS public database / eJustice online pre-check
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search on the RCS electronic register for identical or confusingly similar names. Select at least three proposed corporate names carrying the suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée'. File the name request through the notary's electronic workspace or the LBR eJustice portal. Ensure the name does not contain terms contrary to Luxembourg public policy or reserved regulated industries.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of the incorporator
Power of attorney for any non-appearing signer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name proposal immediately. The refusal may be challenged before the administrative courts of Luxembourg within one month of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a blocked capital account at a Luxembourg bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution and its AML/KYC compliance department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage an authorized Luxembourg bank to open a 'compte bloqué' (blocked account) in the name of the company to be formed. Provide the provisional statutory draft, final corporate purpose covering ISIC 4633 wholesale trade and storage of whole and skimmed milk powder, and source-of-funds documentation. The bank will perform AML/KYC verification and issue a capital-blocking certificate confirming receipt of at least EUR 12,000.
required_dossiers: Passport / ID of all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
Business plan and intended commercial activity statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a supplemental KYC request, provide the requested documentation within the specified time period. If the application is rejected, select an alternate Luxembourg credit institution and restart the AML/KYC process; no RCS filing can occur without the capital blocking certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary appointed by the incorporators; Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the French-language articles of association with the notary. All founding shareholders must appear before the notary in person or by authenticated power of attorney. The notary verifies legal capacity, capital subscription and payment, registered office address, AML declarations and the validity of the corporate purpose. The deed is read to signatories, who sign it; the notary authenticates the act and provides an authenticated electronic copy for the RCS.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association in final form
Capital blocking certificate from the Luxembourg bank
Passport / ID of shareholders and managers
Proof of registered office address or draft lease agreement
Power of attorney for any represented shareholder
Corporate resolutions and constitutional documents if a corporate shareholder is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal defect in the draft, existing signatures are cancelled and a corrected deed is executed. Any dispute over notarial fees is referred to the Chambre des Notaires for mediation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing and registration with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the eJustice electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the authenticated deed electronically with the RCS together with the required annexes. The RCS legal registrar performs a compliance review on legal form, headline purpose and appointment of managers. Upon approval, the RCS issues the registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and records the company in the official commercial register.
required_dossiers: Declaration of acceptance of office by the manager(s)
Copy of the capital blocking certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or refusal, the notary corrects the deed and resubmits within the prescribed deadline. The company may apply for written reasons and lodge an administrative appeal before the competent Minister or the administrative court within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and release of registered extracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS / Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful RCS registration, the RCS automatically publishes the mandatory legal notice in RESA. Obtain the certified RCS extract (extrait du registre de commerce et des sociétés) and verify the registered office, directors, capital, corporate purpose and registration number. This certified extract is the basis for tax, VAT, social security and food operator licensing.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains an error, submit a written rectification request to LBR with the authenticated deed. Unjustified denial may be appealed to the administrative courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social security, business licence and food operator filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Ministère de l'Économie - Direction de l'autorisation d'établissement; Administration vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the certified RCS extract, apply for the corporate tax identification number and VAT number with the AED and ACD, register as an employer with the CCSS, apply for the commercial establishment licence (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011, and obtain food business operator registration with ALVA before storing or trading whole or skimmed milk powder.
required_dossiers: Identification of managers and beneficial owners
Alimentary operator registration form with ALVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business establishment licence is not issued within the statutory deadline, file a formal reminder to the Ministry of the Economy and pursue a deemed-approval claim if provided by law. Tax, VAT and food operator refusals are each subject to written complaint and administrative or judicial appeal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction de l'autorisation d'établissement; Administration vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA) under the Ministry of Agriculture, Viticulture and Rural Development; Administration de l'environnement for classified establishments.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment licence) and Enregistrement sanitaire / agrément en tant qu'établissement du secteur alimentaire under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and Luxembourg national food law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified establishment – Category 4 notification/registration under the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments. No full environmental impact assessment is required for wholesale trading and dry warehouse storage of milk powder without milk processing or livestock rearing. The use of ammonia-based refrigeration systems above the regulatory power threshold would upgrade the installation to a prior operating-authorisation category.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: sanitary and wash-down effluent must meet the municipal sewer by-law or, where no sewer connection exists, the Grand-Ducal water protection thresholds: BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/l, COD ≤ 125 mg/l, TSS ≤ 35 mg/l, pH 6.5–9.0. Volatile organic compounds are limited to below 2 tonnes per year; any bagging/dedusting exhaust must be filtered and kept below 10 mg/Nm³ of particulates. Damaged milk powder lots and packaging must be handled as non-hazardous waste, with a five-year waste register kept on site. Refrigeration equipment must be free of ozone-depleting substances and controlled under EU F-gas Regulation (EU) No 517/2014.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance through the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de sauvetage (CGDIS) and communal fire prevention services covering alarm systems, fire extinguishers, emergency exits and evacuation plans; structural load inspection of racking and storage areas by an approved inspection body (bureau de contrôle agréé); workplace occupational clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering manual handling, PPE, workstation safety and first aid provision.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg – Value Added Tax is administered by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), 1-3 Avenue Guillaume, L-1651 Luxembourg; direct taxes are administered by the Administration des contributions directes (ACD), 33 Rue de la Congrégation, L-1352 Luxembourg; all official registrations, declarations, and taxpayer communications are channelled through the MyGuichet.lu professional portal and the eCDF electronic filing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities: (1) before making any taxable supply in Luxembourg, file VAT registration Form 1 with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu Espace professionnel, attaching power of attorney, constitutional documents, proof of foreign tax residence, and projected Luxembourg turnover; (2) the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits, normally within 5-10 business days; (3) if a fixed establishment or branch is created, register the branch with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) to obtain the corporate matricule, and obtain a business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) where applicable; (4) for direct tax purposes, a non-resident entity with Luxembourg-source business income or a permanent establishment must register with the ACD (Forms 660/670) and file annual corporate income tax and municipal business tax returns; resident SARLs are registered automatically upon notarial incorporation and obtain both the matricule and VAT number ex officio.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – The SARL (société à responsabilité limitée) is a legally opaque Luxembourg-resident capital company subject to corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC), the solidarity surcharge, net wealth tax, and VAT. From 1 January 2025 the CIT headline rate is 16%, the solidarity surcharge is 7% of CIT, and the ICC in Luxembourg City is approximately 6.75%, producing an aggregate combined rate of approximately 23.87%. Resident companies are taxed on worldwide income with relief for foreign permanent-establishment income; the SARL is not pass-through eligible, and the wholesale dairy commodity trade is ordinary commercial income not situated in any tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid transparency election exists; fiscal classification is determined mandatorily by legal form. Available elections and regimes include: (i) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 61 of the VAT law for closely linked Luxembourg-established persons; (ii) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR, permitting CIT and ICC consolidation among companies in a 95% direct or indirect ownership chain; (iii) option to tax certain VAT-exempt supplies, such as immovable property leasing, under Article 50 of the VAT law; (iv) EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS/IOSS) registration for EU distance sales and certain B2C services; (v) SOPARFI participation exemption, which applies automatically by statute to qualifying dividends and capital gains without election; and (vi) mandatory application of ATAD and EU anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the Law of 21 December 2018, with no elective carve-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA) – harmonised with Council Directive 2006/112/EC and the EU customs union export regime
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for non-established foreign entities – VAT registration is mandatory before the first taxable supply in Luxembourg. Resident small traders may claim the Article 57 VAT small-business franchise for annual turnover below EUR 35,000 (excluding construction services); the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold applies to intra-Community distance sales of goods; intra-Community acquisitions by a taxable person below EUR 10,000 per annum do not trigger Luxembourg VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured B2B e-invoicing applies under the Law of 15 July 2023 (draft law n. 8032) and its implementing regulation: from 1 January 2025, all Luxembourg-established taxable persons must be able to receive structured electronic invoices; from 1 January 2026, they must issue structured e-invoices for domestic B2B supplies. The mandated format is EN 16931 / PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0, transmitted via PEPPOL access points or compliant digital transmission platforms; Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction controls (CTC) model, and no QR stamping or government pre-clearance of invoices is required. VAT returns (monthly or quarterly) and EU recapitulative statements must be filed electronically through the eCDF portal, and wholesale commodity traders must maintain SAF-T-compatible accounting records for audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export supplies of raw whole and skimmed milk powder (HS 0402.10 / 0402.21) to non-EU buyers qualify for the 0% VAT rate (exemption with right to deduct input VAT) under Article 54 of the Luxembourg VAT law if: (i) the goods physically leave EU customs territory within the statutory period, generally within three months of the supply date; (ii) the export is validated by an EU customs export declaration accepted and released through the Automated Export System (AES) with exit confirmation; (iii) the sale is made to a non-EU consignee and the transport is performed by the supplier, a third party, or the foreign purchaser; (iv) the supplier obtains and retains the complete documentary evidence file. Where goods are held in customs warehousing or in the Luxembourg Freeport prior to export, VAT may be suspended until the export zero-rating is substantiated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU – Document Administratif Unique) accepted and released through the EU Automated Export System (AES), including the Export Control Reference (ECR) and exit confirmation
Bill of Lading (ocean), CMR waybill (road), or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate – SWIFT/MT103 bank credit evidence proving receipt of the export sale proceeds
Commercial Invoice stating Incoterms, HS code 0402.10/0402.21, quantities, weights, and values
Purchase order or export sales contract, together with packing list
T1 transit declaration or customs warehouse exit records where the export movement used transit suspension
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may audit export zero-rating claims within the standard five-year VAT assessment limitation period, extended to ten years in cases of fraud or serious irregularity. Failure to produce the complete export documentation bundle within the administrative deadline leads to denial of the 0% rate and assessment of VAT at 16% on the invoice value, plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month and administrative penalties under the Luxembourg General Tax Law ranging from EUR 250 up to EUR 100,000; proven fraudulent export claims expose the taxpayer to criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Retrospective clawback also disallows the corresponding input VAT deductions, reinstates net wealth tax and corporate income tax adjustments, and may trigger an extended statute of limitations and publication of the penalty decision.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and under the prudential/compliance framework of the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Supervisory Authority of Luxembourg (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility is guaranteed for both current and capital account transactions under the EU Treaty framework on free movement of capital, the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements, and the Luxembourg Law of 19 March 2004 on the status of the BCL. There are no exchange-control restrictions on profit repatriation, dividend distribution, repayment of shareholder loans, or settlement of trade obligations. The sole fiction is that all cross-border payments exceeding EUR 125,000 must be declared to the BCL for statistical balance-of-payments data (BOP filings); such reporting is not an approval gate, but a post-period openness requirement, and non-filing can result in late penalties after the 15th business day of the following month. In practice, foreign investors must brief their paying bank with the applicable EU BOP purpose code at the time of transfer to avoid administrative delay.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory repatriation period, and no conversion ratio requiring export receipts to be surrendered to the BCL or any licensed bank. Dairy commodity exporters may retain EUR, USD, or third-currency balances in any SEPA-connected or SWIFT-connected account. The only obligation is the standard commercial accounting requirement to book invoiced receivables in EUR for financial statement purposes and to observe any bank-negotiated repayment covenants on trade finance facilities. As a Eurozone Member State, there is no central-bank obligation to convert export proceeds into EUR; however, if the SARL incurs a natural FX risk on USD-denominated receipts and EUR-denominated costs, the treasury risk must be managed voluntarily with permitted hedging instruments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Trade Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for SEPA-denominated in/out flows and ordinary corporate disbursements, but Low-Medium for agricultural commodity trade requiring SWIFT MT103/LC issuance. Licensed electronic-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions under the PSD2/CSSF regime in Luxembourg are legal and passportable across the EEA. They may efficiently onboard the SARL and provide multi-currency e-money wallets, but they cannot legally extend credit, issue documentary letters of credit, or act as clearing agents for large physical milk-powder trade settlements. For the expected trade size, a tier-1 credit institution remains mandatory; fintech rails should be considered only for ancillary working-capital movements, not for primary clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, for a newly formed SARL with non-resident directors and a corporate, non-EU shareholding chain, tier-1 Luxembourg banks require physical attendance of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and at least one managing director for an in-person interview at the bank's registered office. Remote opening using video-verification and Advanced Electronic Signatures is legally permissible under the CSSF AML/CFT circulars, but for trade flows involving documentary credits and a capital escrow release schedule, the prevailing de facto standard is either (i) a personal visit by the UBO to Luxembourg City, or (ii) an intermediary private-banking introduction accompanied by embassy-notarised identity documents. Remote-only onboarding for a cross-border dairy trading entity is rare and, where accepted, is conditioned on enhanced due-diligence, certification of business intent, and a shortened transaction value limit until physical meeting can occur.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain involves a non-resident holding company in a jurisdiction without fully automated beneficial-ownership access, coupled with a 25%+ indirect shareholder structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled register of shareholder ledger; scanned corporate registry excerpts (LBR, RCS) for every intermediate vehicle; an explicit UBO declaration form compliant with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) law; source-of-wealth statement signed by the UBO; 3 years of bank statements and audited financial statements of the immediate direct shareholders; tax-office issued residency certificates for all natural-person UBOs; and a detailed corporate-group organogram with percentage markings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade flows are structured through multiple jurisdictions with high sanctions-transaction velocity and no physical presence of the goods in the SARL's own warehouse, raising red flags on invoice trading or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full merchanting trade contract with counterparty bank references; original factory-issued commercial invoices and packing lists; independent warehouse inventory reports (e.g., SGS or Bureau Veritas) confirming the raw milk powder lot; CMR/Bill of Lading and customs declarations; SWIFT MT103 or MT700 trail from a previous 12-month period showing genuine commodity movements; letter from the Luxembourg trade association confirming ISIC 4633 activity; and a written treasury manual demonstrating that payments are disbursed only against verified title documents under a standard documentary collection / LC process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SARL receives a capital injection on the same day as initial onboarding without a clear commercial rationale, triggering reliance-on-privately-sourced-funds scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share-subscription instrument; bank confirmation of the original remitting account in the shareholder's name; shareholders' resolution allocating funds to transaction operations; confirmation from a Luxembourg notary that the minimum capital contribution has been registered; a cash-flow projection for first-quarter dairy purchases; and a certified copy of the shareholder's board minutes approving the capital injection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (i) all capital contributions exceeding EUR 1,000 must be remitted via wire from an account held in the name of the registered shareholder, no cash or third-party payments; (ii) use SWIFT MT103 for large amounts (EUR 50,000+), otherwise SEPA CT is acceptable for EUR-dominated contributions from EEA account holders; (iii) include the BCL statistical purpose code for direct investment capital participation — accepted codes are 'D.1.1.1' (quoted and unquoted shares) or 'D.1.2.1' (repayment of equity-financing liabilities) as applicable; (iv) attach an opening brief containing the notarised incorporation deed, registration with the Luxembourg Registre de Commerce (RCS), and the bank's own compliance form; (v) mandatory attribution: the credit to the account must be titled 'Capital Contribution under Articles of Incorporation' with the transaction reference
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.? Actually we need a plain string. Let's: in the originator-to-beneficiary information field. All incoming telegrams will be blocked if the account name or purpose is not matched to the SARL's RCS registration. In case of initial contribution from a parent company outside the EU, a file with the consolidated group structure and tax transparency memos must be lodged; otherwise the bank can freeze the transfer pending further documents.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For dairy commodity purchases, the primary clearing rails are: (i) direct documentary letters of credit (LC) governed by UCP 600, the bank issuing a commercial LC to the seller's bank in Switzerland, Belgium, or overseas, covering shipment of blank milk powder (HS 0402.10 / 0402.21); (ii) SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for the post-shipment settlement, with purpose code 'Trade in Goods — Imports' (BOP code 'G.2.1') where the underlying invoice refers to ISIC 4633; (iii) SWIFT MT101 for direct operator-originated payments from the SARL's account; (iv) risk-reducing contingent MT798/MT799 guarantees for quality-quantity warranties. For transactions with Turkish or African buyers, a confirmed LC from a first-class EU bank is the standard instrument to avoid cross-border non-payment risk. Settlement currency is EUR for intra-EEA counterparties and USD for international counterparties, with EUR/USD conversion executed only through the account-holding bank or an approved FX broker.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable over-the-counter (OTC) EUR/USD FX forwards entered into pursuant to an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or local master FX agreement with a licensed credit institution or investment firm, subject to EMIR mandatory clearing/screening at the clearing threshold if the aggregate notional exceeds the applicable CSSF/ESMA thresholds.
Direct EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, and EUR/GBP FX swaps used only for cash-flow management, aligned with the SARL's documented treasury policy and subject to BOP reporting thresholds.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for multi-year USDA-denominated dairy supply contracts, where the notional exchange is physically settled at maturity; such swaps are permissible only where the rationale is hedging the currency risk on the underlying commodity trade and are not permitted for speculative directional carry.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in currencies subject to offshore restrictions (e.g., CNY) — permissible only for hedging genuine trade flows denominated in that currency, and must be entered into with a Luxembourg-authorised credit institution or a validly passporting EU bank; any NDF must be documented with the underlying trade invoice to avoid recharacterisation as a regulated leveraged derivative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts and List of Shareholders (Comptes Annuels et Liste des Associés) filed with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the close of the financial year; for a calendar-year SARL, mandatory filing by 30 June of the following year; accounts must be approved by shareholders before filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interested parties or the public prosecutor may petition the Commercial Tribunal to order the filing under a coercive fine (astreinte); persistent non-filing can lead to judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCS; criminal fines may also be imposed under Article 14 of the Law of 19 December 2002

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Ownership (Confirmation Annuelle des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary of the initial registration in the RBE; must be filed annually even if no beneficial ownership change occurred; any change requires a separate filing within one month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers and the company are liable to criminal sanctions prescribed by the Law of 13 January 2019, including fines of EUR 250 up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment for serious breaches; continued non-compliance blocks the issuance of RBE compliance certificates and may impair RCS filings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following thresholds on two consecutive balance-sheet dates: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce of 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory for public issuers, credit institutions, insurance undertakings, and any company required by its articles or by shareholder decision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 19 December 2002 on companies, the RCS and annual accounts (as amended, incorporating Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU is mandatory for listed issuers and may be applied to consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file an annual confirmation with the RBE within one month after the anniversary of its initial UBO declaration. The confirmation restates the identity, nationality, residential address, and nature and extent of beneficial interest of each beneficial owner. This filing is required despite the absence of any change; all changes must also be filed within one month of becoming known. The internal UBO register must be kept at the registered office and continuously updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (list of SARL associates and shareholdings)
Register of Directors / Managers (appointments, revocations, and decisions)
Minute Book (minutes of general meetings and management resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 – 4,000 per annum for registered office provision, statutory correspondence handling, and corporate secretarial services via a licensed fiduciary or PFS
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 15,000 per annum if audit thresholds are exceeded; no statutory audit fee is required for a below-threshold SARL absent shareholder request

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% effective aggregate rate in Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (0%); IP box allowing 80% exemption of qualified IP income; investment tax credit for eligible fixed assets; no general CIT holiday for commercial trading companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu / corporation income tax return) filed electronically via Luxembourg eCDF portal on MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year companies the tax administration normally requires filing by 31 December of the following year; extension available upon reasoned request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, legal form, Luxembourg registered office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert legal form 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée'; where a non-resident owns the SARL, identify the ultimate beneficial owner and their tax residence in an annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg RCS number is unchanged for non-resident owners; attach certified incorporation documents to the first filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period opening and closing dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg entity must close its own annual accounts on a 12-month basis; a non-resident group parent may prepare consolidation packs on a different year-end only for audit purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after commercial and tax adjustments, including disallowed expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border commodity trading income is taxable at the SARL's place of effective management in Luxembourg; if the SARL is administered from abroad, the return should disclose the foreign management office and reflect a Luxembourg taxable permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption declaration for qualifying dividends and capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the holding threshold (at least 10% or acquisition price of EUR 1.2 million) and the 12-month uninterrupted holding period; provide legalised share certificates and foreign tax confirmation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing schedules: intra-group transactions, counterparties, values, and the pricing methodology used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When a non-resident group member is the counterparty, attach the Local File, Master File schedule, and any Advance Pricing Agreement; include all related dairy commodity traders in NL, CH, UAE, and other jurisdictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding taxes suffered on Luxembourg-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not claim WHT relief in the SARL's income tax return; shareholders apply separately for restitution using Form 105.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carryforward position used in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident acquirer changes the ownership of the SARL, evidence ownership continuity to preserve the loss carryforward; termination of the business activity forfeits the losses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EUR 25 to EUR 2,500 per offence; default assessment issued by the tax office; monthly default interest of 0.8% on unpaid tax; recalcitrant penalties up to EUR 25,000, rising to EUR 250,000 for knowingly incomplete or fraudulent declarations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 520 (Net Wealth Tax return – Impôt sur la Fortune) filed via the same Luxembourg eCDF electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline aligned to the CIT return deadline (31 December following the fiscal year-end; extensions available on request).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable net wealth: net accounting assets, less exempt participation holdings and non-deductible liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg SARL is taxable on its worldwide net wealth except assets connected with a foreign permanent establishment; non-resident shareholders do not owe Luxembourg net wealth tax in respect of the SARL shares.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Minimum net wealth tax schedule: EUR 1,500 standard; EUR 250 for dormant companies and certain holding companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the minimum net wealth tax even if the company has no operating activity; if financial assets represent more than 90% of total assets and are not traded, the minimum tax may rise to EUR 3,210.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 520 triggers the immediate minimum net wealth tax plus daily fines as notified; unpaid net wealth tax bears 0.8% monthly interest; the late filing penalties applicable to Form 510 apply mutatis mutandis.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; 0% for dividends meeting the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and the Luxembourg participation exemption (holding at least 10% or an investment of at least EUR 1.2 million held for an uninterrupted 12-month period).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Apply to reduce Luxembourg withholding tax at source using Form 105 or the DTA exemption certificate ('titre d'exemption'); the Luxembourg tax office must approve before the payment date. File a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority, a beneficial ownership declaration, shareholding register extracts, and holding-period affidavits. If not approved in time, withhold at 15% and file a refund request after the tax year; the TRC must state that the shareholder is fiscally resident in the treaty state and does not have a fixed base in Luxembourg through which the shareholding is effectively connected.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes 0% withholding tax on outgoing royalty and interest payments. Under applicable income tax treaties, royalty rates generally fall between 0% and 10%; interest is commonly subject to 0% WHT. Beneficial ownership and substantive business reasons remain decisive to avoid anti-abuse clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File triggered when aggregate intra-group transactions of the Luxembourg entity exceed EUR 1,000,000 in a fiscal year; Master File required where the consolidated group revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000 (the CbCR threshold). Documentation must be contemporaneous and drafted in English, French, or German.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a UAE-style ESR schedule, but it enforces economic substance through the OECD substance doctrine, the Luxembourg anti-abuse clause, EU ATAD, and Circulars LIR 56/1 and LIR 56bis-1. To secure treaty benefits and participation exemption, the trading SARL must demonstrate local staffing, strategic decision-making, operational risk, and physical office presence. A letterbox company without genuine substance is denied treaty relief and subject to retroactive reclassification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Deliberate Under-Declaration and Fraudulent Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-declaring revenue from whole and skimmed milk powder sales, fabricating invoices, or creating a circular flow of cash through non-treaty jurisdictions to evade Luxembourg corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg tax fraud penalties: fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years, plus an administrative surcharge of 10% to 100% of the evaded tax depending on gravity, monthly late-payment interest of 0.8%, and automatic rejection of deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors may be held personally liable for the SARL's unpaid tax up to the amount of the tax debt when they knowingly file false returns; criminal courts may order a travel ban, asset freeze, and a professional ban of up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Luxembourg SARL as a letterbox company without local premises, employees, books, or decision-making; executing commodity trades with a related party located in a low-substance jurisdiction; retaining no control over inventory, logistics, or commercial risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authorities disregard the corporate veil, reallocate all Luxembourg-source commodity profits to the beneficial owner, deny treaty and participation exemption, impose an additional net wealth tax assessment, and levy a civil fine up to EUR 25,000; registration in the RCS may be struck off.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors allowing the company to operate as a shell become jointly responsible for corporate liabilities if the company is clearly insolvent; the court may order liquidation, directorship disqualification, and personal civil liability for the unpaid tax and damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Violation / Unsatisfactory Contemporaneous Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing dairy powdered-milk trading margins below arm's length to a related purchaser; failing to file the mandatory Local File after EUR 1,000,000 in intra-group transactions; switching between CUP and TNMM ex post to achieve low tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax office may adjust the taxable margin to an arm's length level, reclassify the difference as a constructive dividend, apply a 10% surcharge for non-reporting, and impose a fine up to EUR 50,000 for missing documentation; default interest runs from the original assessment's due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing declarations may be personally assessed for the additional tax under the directors' civil negligence standard; administrative sanctions may include removal from office and a ban from board membership in a Luxembourg company for at least five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership Non-Compliance in Cross-Border Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Undertaking SWIFT LC or TT wire payments without customer due diligence or KYC on non-resident beneficiaries; failing to disclose the UBO in Luxembourg's register; transacting with sanctions-linked dairy traders; structuring payments below EUR denominated thresholds to avoid AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF regulations: criminal imprisonment of up to five years and a fine up to EUR 1,250,000; administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; automatic withdrawal of the commodity-trading license relevant to ISIC 4633 dairy distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in AML breaches are liable for damages to the company and third parties, may be subject to travel bans pending criminal investigation, and can be barred from exercising any corporate mandate for up to 10 years; personal bankruptcy and asset confiscation may be ordered in severe cases.
